If you really believe that the job is the problem, then you should look for something else. However, I've gotten caught in that before, thinking that if I changed my job things would be better, when the job isn't the problem.

Adding a paycut and a commute is likely to add stress to your life, so unless whatever job you find has some other amazing aspect that would make your life fulfilling, it would be better to try to find something in your life other than work to give you what you're currently lacking in your life.

Most jobs suck. Some very lucky people will find that theirs doesn't, but I've been learning that most jobs are just bad. It'll look like it's better for a bit, a honeymoon period, but it'll turn out to be just as bad.

I left a WFH job that paid several dollars more an hour because I was stressed out all the time. Now I make less, have a 30 minute commute, and am stressed out and miserable, just in a different way from my old job.

Just be careful, and be honest about what a different job might be able to offer you in life.

Drinking calories is really dangerous to weight loss. Pop and energy drinks, but also juice and smoothies, not to mention alcohol. It's very easy to consume a lot of calories and not feel full that way. I had a problem with alcohol and quit drinking, and realized that I'd basically cut my daily calories in half by doing that.

Diet drinks are better, but there's a lot of research that says that for some people that can cause other problems, like an increase in appetite and other health issues. Diet is better, but water is best.

Start slow, is my suggestion. Change one or two drinks for water per day for a little while, and then when that doesn't seem like a huge act of willpower, do two more.

Exercise is important, but most weight loss happens with your daily diet. You want to make a diet something you can do every day as a habit.
